description: Registered suppressions. Every live suppression directive (oxlint, eslint, ts-expect-error, ts-ignore, ts-nocheck, @effect-diagnostics) must match an entry by file and directive, and every entry needs a live suppression. An entry names its scope, reason, native alternatives examined, owner, versions and retirement trigger.

exceptions.reason: The Cloudflare Workers host ABI is Promise-based: a Durable Object's RPC methods and `alarm()` and a Worker's `fetch` are `async` methods that the runtime calls. `asyncFunction:off` applies to this one file, the boundary adapter between that ABI and one ManagedRuntime per host (spec 0000, D11 and Revisions 5); every method body is one `runtime.runPromise` of an Effect, so no domain logic is async. The file-level `oxlint-disable` covers the same host: `effect/no-native-promise-control-flow` and `effect/no-premature-execution` (the host builds its two ManagedRuntimes), and the global `Cloudflare.Env` augmentation that types `env` from `cloudflare:workers` (`no-namespace`, `no-empty-interface`, `no-empty-object-type`, `consistent-type-imports`).
nativeAlternativesExamined: Alchemy v2's Effect-native Durable Object (`DurableObjectShape` with Effect-valued `fetch` and `alarm`): it hides the async ABI, but `Lifecycle.install(host)` of PiHarness (spec 0001) needs a real `cloudflare:workers` DurableObject class, and a local workerd smoke test needs no Alchemy tooling with a plain class.
Effect.promise / Effect.callback around the handlers: they wrap calls from Effect into Promises, the reverse of what the host needs; the host must return Promises to the platform.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: Cloudflare's runtime accepts Effect-valued handlers directly, or this host moves to Alchemy's Effect-native Durable Object (if spec 0001 does not need the class form).
